title: AI Governance for Firms
summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance, risk, model risk and technology staff the tools to design, run and evidence robust AI governance across the firm.
intro: This training programme equips compliance, risk, model risk, data and technology staff with the practical tools to design, run and evidence robust AI governance across the firm, seeing its AI the way a supervisor does.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip the people who build, validate and control AI in a regulated firm with a working understanding of how AI systems are developed and fail, and with the governance, model risk and control tools to manage them. Participants leave able to design and operate the firm's AI framework, document and validate models to a standard that withstands scrutiny, and evidence sound control to supervisors and auditors.
sections.What It Covers: AI and machine learning foundations, the firm's AI governance framework, model risk management and explainability, bias and fairness testing, AI in trading and operations, AI in advice and client-facing tools, vulnerabilities and third-party AI risk, regulatory expectations across jurisdictions, AI for the firm's own compliance and risk functions, and embedding AI governance across the firm.
Intended Audience: Compliance, risk and legal professionals responsible for AI policy, oversight and regulatory compliance
Model risk, model validation, data science and technology staff who build, buy or run AI systems
Senior managers and business-line owners accountable for AI use cases and their outcomes
Learning Objectives: Explain how machine learning and generative AI systems are built, trained and deployed, and the risks each stage introduces
Design an AI governance framework, inventory and accountability structure fit for the firm's scale and use cases
Apply model risk management, explainability and fairness testing to the firm's AI models
Implement controls, kill-switches and escalation for AI used in trading, operations and client-facing services
Assess AI vulnerabilities, vendor dependency and regulatory obligations across the jurisdictions in which the firm operates
Evidence effective AI governance to supervisors and auditors and agree an action plan for the firm
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines technical grounding with case studies, group exercises and practical templates, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's use cases.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, risk, model development or technology in a regulated firm is helpful. No data science background is required.
Core Reading: NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
IOSCO, The Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning by Market Intermediaries and Asset Managers (2021)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)

modules.title: Foundations of AI and Machine Learning
modules.summary: The technical grounding needed to engage credibly with AI governance: how models are built, trained and deployed, how generative AI differs from traditional approaches, and what each choice means for risk.
objectives: Explain how supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning models are built and deployed
Distinguish statistical models, machine learning and generative AI, and their risk implications
Assess the governance trade-offs between building AI in-house and buying from vendors
syllabus: The AI system lifecycle: data, training, testing, deployment and retirement
Statistics, machine learning and large language models compared
Build versus buy: accountability for vendor and third-party AI
Documenting the business case for an AI use case

modules.title: Building the Firm's AI Governance Framework
modules.summary: How the firm designs and operates an AI governance framework, from board accountability to day-to-day oversight, with the policies, inventory and lines of defence that give credible assurance.
objectives: Design a framework that allocates clear accountability from the board to the business line
Develop an AI policy, risk appetite statement and firm-wide model inventory
Structure the three lines of defence for AI risk, including independent validation
syllabus: Board and senior management accountability for AI outcomes
AI policy, risk appetite, use-case approval and the model inventory
Principles in practice: fairness, transparency and meaningful human oversight
Common governance weaknesses and how supervisors spot them

modules.title: Model Risk Management and Explainability
modules.summary: Extending the firm's model risk framework to machine learning and generative AI, with the interpretation techniques, documentation, validation and monitoring standards that withstand internal and external scrutiny.
objectives: Apply interpretation techniques such as feature importance and counterfactual explanations
Extend model risk management to machine learning and generative AI
Design documentation, independent validation and ongoing monitoring for AI models
syllabus: Black-box models and practical interpretation techniques
Explainability needs by use case, from credit decisions to trading
Documentation and validation standards before and after deployment
Drift monitoring, retraining and model retirement protocols

modules.title: Bias, Fairness and Customer Outcomes
modules.summary: Building bias and fairness testing into the model development lifecycle, weighing fairness metrics and trade-offs, and meeting consumer protection and non-discrimination obligations in the firm's own decisioning.
objectives: Explain how historical data, proxies and feedback loops introduce bias
Apply fairness metrics and evaluate the trade-offs between them
Design bias testing and outcome monitoring across the model lifecycle
syllabus: Sources of bias: historical data, proxy discrimination and feedback loops
Fairness metrics in credit scoring, insurance pricing and targeting
Fair treatment and non-discrimination obligations applied to AI decisions
Case studies of AI bias harms and the governance failures behind them

modules.title: AI in Trading, Investment and Operations
modules.summary: Controls for AI used in algorithmic trading, portfolio construction and operational processing, the market integrity risks it can introduce, and the kill-switches and escalation the firm must build.
objectives: Explain how AI is used in trading, portfolio construction, signal generation and processing
Assess market integrity risks, including correlated behaviour and flash events
Design kill-switches, human oversight and escalation for AI-driven systems
syllabus: AI in algorithmic and high-frequency trading
AI-driven portfolio construction, risk tools and reconciliation
Market integrity risks: correlated behaviour, flash events and algorithmic collusion
Designing kill-switches, limits and escalation protocols

modules.title: AI in Advice and Client-Facing Services
modules.summary: Designing robo-advice, chatbots and personalisation tools that meet suitability, disclosure and record-keeping obligations, treat customers fairly and stay on the right side of the guidance versus advice boundary.
objectives: Explain how automated advice, chatbots and virtual assistants are designed and deployed
Apply suitability, disclosure and record-keeping requirements to automated processes
Evaluate personalisation and dynamic pricing against fair treatment obligations
syllabus: Robo-advice and automated portfolio recommendations
Chatbots and generative AI assistants in service and sales
Guidance versus regulated advice in AI-enabled client tools
Fair treatment risks in personalisation and dynamic pricing

modules.title: AI Vulnerabilities, Resilience and Third-Party Risk
modules.summary: Identifying and managing vulnerabilities in the firm's AI estate, from silent degradation to adversarial attack, with vendor due diligence, resilience testing and incident response for when things go wrong.
objectives: Identify drift, data quality degradation and silent failure modes
Assess exposure to adversarial attacks, data poisoning and prompt injection
Design vendor due diligence, resilience testing and incident response for AI
syllabus: Drift, data degradation and silent failures
Adversarial attacks, data poisoning and prompt injection
Vendor and foundation-model dependency, concentration and exit planning
Resilience testing, scenario analysis and AI incident response

modules.title: AI Regulation and Supervisory Expectations
modules.summary: How jurisdictions are regulating AI, how AI-specific rules overlay existing financial services obligations, and how the firm evidences compliance when operating across several regimes.
objectives: Explain the main approaches to AI regulation and the duties they place on providers and deployers
Identify which of the firm's AI uses are likely to be treated as high-risk
Evidence compliance to financial supervisors and other authorities
syllabus: Approaches to AI regulation: risk-based laws, sectoral rules and supervisory guidance
International frameworks: OECD, NIST, ISO/IEC 42001, IOSCO, FSB and BIS
Overlay with conduct, prudential, consumer and data protection rules
Managing divergence across jurisdictions and preparing for supervisory reviews

modules.title: AI for the Firm's Own Compliance and Risk Functions
modules.summary: Using AI and RegTech tools to strengthen the firm's compliance monitoring, surveillance and regulatory reporting, and the data, governance and skills foundations needed to get real value from them.
objectives: Explain how RegTech supports compliance monitoring, surveillance and reporting
Apply anomaly detection, network analysis and dashboards within the compliance function
Assess the data, governance and skills foundations required for effective adoption
syllabus: RegTech for compliance monitoring and regulatory reporting
AI-enabled surveillance, anomaly detection and network analysis
Compliance dashboards and management information
Data quality, governance and in-house skills for adoption

modules.title: Embedding AI Governance Across the Firm
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a firm-wide approach covering capability, culture, generative AI and autonomous agents, keeping the framework current and evidencing it to supervisors.
objectives: Embed AI oversight consistently across business, risk, compliance and technology functions
Evaluate governance questions raised by generative AI and autonomous agents
Produce a prioritised action plan for the firm's AI governance
syllabus: Building AI capability: skills, tools and organisational placement
Generative AI and autonomous agents: accountability and control
Seeing the firm's AI the way a supervisor does: evidence and readiness
Workshop: the firm's twelve-month AI governance action plan
